findings.reason: The unit moved reactions to take `rootId` from the binding's `ReactionInput` (`reactionRootId(source, input)` in the M06/M08/M14/M17 handlers), but two reactions bound by the same loop still parse it from the source name: `m02-frontmatter-indexer` (`requireRootId(source)` here and at :83) and the base `m02-file-changed` (`fileChangedNotifier`, src/server/fs/notifications.ts:25), which is the reaction that emits `file:changed {rootId,...}`. Today the two answers are the same only because `ARTIFACT_ROOT_ID` in sources.ts happens to equal the system root ids. Two ways to get one value in the same loop will drift. Switch both to `reactionRootId(source, input)`, or say in a comment why these two are exempt (the comment in sources.ts that says the suffix serves 'the base notification' describes a handler that is in fact bound with an input).

The doc comment says the positional `(cwd, dir, rootId)` constructor is 'kept for the hand-rolled rigs (tests, the serverless discovery reader)', but this same diff moved the discovery reader (src/server/discovery/page-source.ts:35) to the `{ root, store }` form, so no production code uses the overload now. Its remaining users are in tests/helpers/test-app.ts:330-334, which build `PagesService` facades for briefs/patches/plans. That is the very construction the unit forbids ('no PagesService outside pages roots'), and the overload also skips the facade/store rootId check. Fix the stale comment, and either move the rig to bare `MarkdownFileStore` instances or record why the overload stays.

A colocated unit test checks build order by running `indexOf` on the raw text of project-context.ts (`'await mountRegistryRoots('`, `'bindRegistryReactions(rootRegistry,'`, `'.indexAll('`). Renaming a variable, reformatting, or matching an `.indexAll(` from some other service breaks it or makes it pass by accident, and none of it tests behaviour. Source scans of this kind belong in tests/integration/architecture/ (as in root-kind-gating.test.ts), not inside the ac-tagged runtime test. Move it there, or drop it in favour of the behavioural assertions above it.

`isHtmlPreviewPath` claims to follow 'whatever the map calls a raw HTML entry' rather than 'an extension check of our own', but it compares `entry.pattern === '**/*.html'`, a hard-coded pattern literal, which is stricter than the old extension check. If the `pages` file map's raw entry ever changes shape (e.g. `**/*.{html,htm}`), previews silently stop refreshing even though the tree still lists those files as `fileType: 'html'`. Use `entry.format === 'raw'`, which is how `PagesService.walk` classifies the same entry.
